releases.notes: A runner's node agent ran at most 16 jobs at once and ignored the rest; with box operations running side by side (0.9.66), a burst of more than 16 left the extra ones unattached, and the controller recorded them uncertain after its 10 s attach wait, so their boxes stayed 'being created' for the 30-minute creation timeout. The agent now runs up to 64 jobs and holds up to 256, each waiting up to 8 s for a slot (under the controller's 10 s attach wait); the controller proxies up to 96 runner jobs at once, all runners together (was 32), and holds up to 64 job IDs per runner for its agent (was 16). A job the runner never took is answered as not dispatched (nothing reached the runner): its operation can be retried with the same key and its box deleted at once. Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime and host layout 2 are unchanged. Class 1: the controller, agent and dashboard restart (seconds); boxes keep running.

Box operations run side by side. The controller holds its catalog only for an operation's bookkeeping: runner inventories are read before the lock is taken and after the runner call, and the call itself runs unlocked, so operations on different boxes overlap (one on the same box waits for the one in flight). Reconcile leaves a box to its in-flight call's result, and does not apply an inventory read before a call on that box started or landed; it applies each runner's inventory in one transaction. A runner boots new boxes off its worker thread: the box's disk and VMM are made on it as before, then filesystem growth, boot and guest setup run on their own thread while the worker takes other requests; requests for a box still booting wait for it; detach, shutdown and quiesce wait for boxes still booting, and one landing after shutdown began is stopped. Runner requests no longer stall about 40 ms each on the node listener (TCP_NODELAY) or poll the worker socket every 10 ms. Placement logs why each runner was passed over when a create finds no room. Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged. Class 2: the worker hands its boxes over and they keep running; the controller and dashboard restart (seconds).

Client upgrades follow the latest release: ow upgrade now targets the release GitHub marks latest (read from the redirect of /releases/latest, so it spends no GitHub API quota), not the controller's GET /api/version, which is the dashboard's release and can lag the release the fleet runs. Before replacing the running client, the downloaded candidate runs its own status against the same controller and must report connected with compatibility.next_action null. If the latest release is not newer, it is a no-op; if its assets, checks or status fail, it falls back to the controller's release and says why, and a candidate that failed after its .sha256 was found is not downloaded again for 10 minutes. A controller reached over the local socket gets its own release, since the candidate's status could not reach it. --version keeps its exact meaning; --check reports the latest release without downloading it. --json adds source (latest, controller or version) and, on a fallback, reason. Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged. Class 0: nothing restarts.

The release workflow no longer depends on GitHub's release notes service: creating the draft release is retried, then made with the commit message as its notes; attaching the clients and publishing the release retry GitHub errors too (each reads the state back, so an answer that was lost is not repeated). Nothing that runs on a host or client changes. Class 0.

A create or fork whose operation row stayed pending (its dispatch failed inside the controller, for example on a locked catalog write) now fails after the 30-minute creation timeout like an uncertain one when the runner has no such machine, so its machine row can be deleted and its reservation goes. Before, only a controller restart freed it. Runner pools no longer count a box whose create failed against `max` while its removal waits, so a refused delete does not take a warm runner's slot.

The dashboard now moves whenever the agent moves (whose restart already drops its streams): it serves the admin API (the controller's settings) and /api/version, which clients upgrade to. Before, a release that changed only the controller or agent left the dashboard on its old release, so a new controller setting (0.9.60's upgrade.running_boxes) was refused as unknown and `ow upgrade` clients kept seeing the old version. This release declares a dashboard change so the upgrader already running moves the dashboard now. Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged. Class 1: the dashboard restarts (seconds); boxes keep running.

Golden image recipes can set the image disk, 1 to 32 GiB: `# ow-image: base=ubuntu disk_gib=8` builds the builder (and so the image) with an 8 GiB root disk instead of the 32 GiB create default. Boxes made from it get 32 GiB unless they ask for another size from the image's up. Local builds use the new ow; controller-dispatched builds run in the node agent, so the agent moves (class 1). No worker, protocol or catalog change.

Runners now follow every change of the controller's upgrade settings: the node agent stored controller-settings.json with a no-clobber write, so only its first value ever landed and each later acknowledgement logged `controller settings: File exists (os error 17)`; it now replaces the file (temporary file and rename) and writes only when a value changes. New controller setting upgrade.running_boxes (hibernate, the default, or stop; config.set over the admin API, delivered with each acknowledgement, stored in the same file): when a worker upgrade or `ow-host restart --worker` cannot hand over, stop has the upgrader stop each running box (journal step stop-boxes, reported as an ow.host.upgrade.step event with the boxes stopped) instead of hibernating it, and start it again after verify, cold; abort, rollback and recover start them too. Managed boxes are still hibernated and ephemeral boxes stopped as before; `--hibernate` forces hibernation; hand-over still wins. `--plan` reports worker_path stop and running_boxes. Abort no longer leaves a host half-upgraded when the old worker exits while it acts (a `down --hibernate` client that timed out): it waits for the worker to answer or exit, starts it if it exited, tries the resume twice and records a failure instead of raising, so the drain, units and timers are restored and the journal reaches aborted. Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel, hand-over format and host layout 2 are unchanged. Class 1: the agent and controller restart; the worker does not, so boxes keep running through this upgrade.

waivers.dashboard: dashboard.rs changes only a test: the worker operations the dashboard refuses now list detach and hibernate-unresponsive

releases.notes: Worker hand-over (ADR 0011): running VMMs outlive a worker restart and the new worker adopts them, so a worker-only upgrade or `ow-host restart --worker` keeps every box running (seconds of downtime, no RAM capture) instead of hibernating it. A VMM, guest kernel or worker unit change still hibernates, as does a failed adoption (per box: an unresponsive VMM is hibernated after verify, one that is gone boots again, cold). Ephemeral boxes are handed over too; on the hibernate path, and when adopted unresponsive, they are stopped as before and never resumed. The upgrader's journal steps handover and adoption are reported as ow.host.upgrade.step events (handover with the boxes handed over). The controller setting upgrade.worker_handover (default true, config.set over the admin API, delivered to runners with each acknowledgement) turns it off; `--hibernate` forces the old path once; runners advertise worker_handover_v1 (ow nodes). The worker unit gets KillMode=process. Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged. Class 2: this upgrade itself still hibernates, since the worker it replaces cannot hand over.

waivers.worker: crates/ow/src/host.rs lists only the new ow upgrade command among those it never dispatches; the worker's own code is unchanged

releases.notes: Client self-update: ow upgrade [--version vX.Y.Z] [--check] [--json] installs the release the configured controller runs (GET /api/version, so no new API op) or the named one. It downloads this platform's published client, refuses it unless its .sha256 matches, SHA256SUMS lists that hash, the header is this platform's executable and it reports the expected version, then renames it over the running binary. It never downgrades unless --version names the release; --check exits 0 when current and 10 when an upgrade is available. Release notify: after publishing, the release workflow sends a repository_dispatch (open-workspaces-release, with tag, commit and version) to each repository in the RELEASE_DISPATCH_REPOS variable, using the RELEASE_DISPATCH_TOKEN secret; a failed dispatch only warns. Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged. Class 0: nothing restarts.

GitHub Actions runner pools (docs/ACTIONS.md): the controller keeps warm single-use GitHub Actions runners registered and idle, each in its own ephemeral box made through a workload token, so a queued job starts as soon as GitHub assigns it; the box is deleted once GitHub drops its runner after the job. Settings actions.pools and actions.github_app_id (read live every 2 s; idle boxes of an old shape are replaced, busy ones finish); admin ops actions.status and actions.app_key.set (the key is kept 0600, never returned, redacted in the audit log); CLI ow actions status and ow actions app-key set. Ephemeral boxes also never get a recovery point (backup recover skips them), and snapshot, fork, restore, image saves and every transfer (move, park, fork to another runner) refuse one before anything is reserved; a drain deletes a stopped ephemeral box instead of parking it. Journals (the controller's operation journal and the runner agent's effect journal) keep a put's file contents only as their SHA-256. Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged. Class 2: the worker restarts through the upgrade policy (0.9.56's chunk-sealed hibernation).

Upgrades and worker restarts fail fast and hibernate faster. A hibernation was sealed with whole-file hashes, so the worker reread a box's entire disk on one thread (about 17 minutes for a 256 GiB disk); the 840 s budget of ow down --hibernate ran out, the client's read timed out (os error 11, Resource temporarily unavailable), every later box got a 1 s budget and the upgrader waited out its fixed 1800 s cap. Hibernations are now chunk-sealed (sha256-chunks, in the chunk size of the box's last durable recovery point), reusing the chunks whose extents that point shares, on up to eight threads. ow down --hibernate stops at the first box that fails or overruns its own budget (120 s + 20 s per GiB of RAM + 4 s per GiB of allocated disk) and calls the shutdown off; the upgrader's cap is the sum of those budgets plus 600 s. Ephemeral boxes (ow create --ephemeral, the create op's ephemeral flag; every box a workload token creates) are never hibernated: idle hibernation skips them, the hibernate op refuses them, and worker restarts and upgrades stop them instead and leave them out of the capture gate and the resume list. The upgrader hands one ow.host.upgrade.step event per step to the host's telemetry intake as each step ends (those the stopped agent missed at the close) and one ow.host.upgrade event when its journal closes; the agent, or on a controller-only host the controller (shown under controller in health.get), stores and forwards them like its other events. ow-aws ci-post-up answers a deploy that changes nothing in one SSM call per host, and after an upgrade applies the config again with the new release's ow-host, so settings the old one did not know are not dropped. A worker service stop still tries every box; ephemeral boxes are stopped after the others hibernated. Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged. Class 2: the worker restarts through the upgrade policy, which on this upgrade still runs the previous release's hibernation.

waivers.worker: host.rs only lists the new admin command among those it never dispatches; the worker's own code is unchanged

releases.notes: Spill: a placement pool whose own runners are full may place up to N boxes on a named runner of another pool, while that runner keeps placement.spill_keep_free_mib of memory for its own pool. Two controller settings, placement.spill (pool:node:max_boxes rules) and placement.spill_keep_free_mib (default 16384), changed with ow config set and read on every create; off by default. Nothing spills while the pool has no live runner of its own. New admin op placement.status (ow placement status) shows each rule's usage and state. Additive catalog table box_pools records each non-default create's pool; catalog schema unchanged. Class 1: the controller and dashboard restart; workers and boxes keep running.

waivers.worker: host.rs only stops dispatching the admin commands, which the CLI now sends to the admin API; the worker's own code is unchanged

releases.notes: Admin API: every operator operation (settings, fleet health, node pools, workload tokens, host invitations) is one audited op on POST /api/admin. The gateway serves it to the designated pool owner over HTTPS; the node controller (or, without one, the dashboard) serves the same op handlers on admin.sock in the controller data directory to root and the controller user. ow config, health, node-pool, token and host invite|budget|revoke are thin wrappers and need that controller running; ow config list and get print the new result objects (settings nested under settings, version beside them). New: ow config history, config set --expect-version. Additive tables admin_audit and admin_operations; catalog schema unchanged. The AWS component's dashboardOwner binds a tailnet login as the gateway's owner once they have signed in. Class 1: the controller and dashboard restart; workers and boxes keep running.

Faster release builds: Rust build caches, the pre-tag checks beside the client builds, and the Intel macOS client cross-built on Apple silicon and checked under Rosetta 2. Hosts install the same clients. Class 0: nothing restarts.

Fresh hosts build their developer images again: the repository's ow wrapper, which experiments/guest-dev/build.py runs, uses the release's own installed bin/ow on a host (RELEASE/src beside RELEASE/bin and RELEASE/assets) instead of target/release/ow, which hosts installed from published binaries never build and which the shared build folder may hold from another release; a developer checkout still uses target/release/ow. Class 0: nothing restarts, and a host upgraded in place keeps its worker's older wrapper until a release moves the worker.

Fresh hosts bootstrap again: scripts/setup-local.sh downloads the pinned rustup-init 1.29.1 from its versioned archive URL instead of dist/ (always the newest rustup), whose new release no longer matched the pinned hash and failed every new runner's staging. The Ubuntu base rootfs comes from its versioned 24.04.5 folder, not the 24.04 folder that drops old point releases. Hosts that already staged a release are unaffected. Class 0: nothing restarts.

Pool admins start, stop, hibernate and resize any owner's box (resize checked against the owner's limits), each audited for the owner; the audit table is rebuilt once to accept the new actions (older readers keep working). Upgrades pause ow-recovery.timer and ow-backup.timer while the journal is open and restore them when it closes; recover() pauses them too; apply leaves them stopped during an open upgrade. The worker answers status (marked busy, live internet) and egress-enable on a separate control thread while a long request such as a snapshot hash holds it. Box disks get virtio-blk discard with rootflags=discard and one background fstrim per cold boot, so freed guest blocks become holes again. developer-images keeps the local image when the store pins none. Class 2: the worker restarts (running boxes hibernate and resume). The upgrade that installs this still runs the previous upgrader: stop ow-recovery.timer by hand first.

Placement pools and workload tokens. ow node-pool RUNNER POOL (controller host) puts a runner in a placement pool; creates reach a runner outside default only when they ask for its pool (ow create --pool, or pool on the create operation) as a pool admin or with a workload token bound to it; moves, forks to a runner, wakes and artifact restores onto such a runner need a pool admin. ow token issue|revoke|list (controller host) manages workload tokens: scoped bearer credentials for a program, bound to one owner and one pool, allowing only create, put, exec, stop and delete on that owner's own boxes through POST /api/operation; stored as SHA-256 in the additive workload_tokens table. Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged. Class 1: the controller and dashboard restart once; running boxes are untouched.

waivers.worker: crates/ow/src/host.rs adds only the local node-pool and token CLI arms and the create --pool refusal; no worker code, operation, runtime or service changes.

releases.notes: Snapshot verification survives restarts and skips holes: the worker keeps the fingerprints of verified snapshots in verified.json (any change to a file changes its fingerprint and forces a new hash) and hashes in process, feeding sparse holes as zeros instead of reading them, so a restarted worker no longer re-reads every snapshot before it answers (issue 90). The upgrader's verify and worker wait allow 1800 s. Caps lifted: a box may have up to 32 vCPUs (Firecracker's limit) on runners that advertise max_guest_vcpus_v2, older peers still see at most 16; host budgets are no longer clamped to 64 GiB, 64 vCPUs or 8 slots (three quarters of RAM, every vCPU, 32 slots); dashboard UI 1.0.2 offers up to 256 GiB and 32 vCPUs. Protocol, catalog schema 7, runtime and guest kernel unchanged. Class 2: the worker restarts behind the capture gate; the budget change re-renders the worker and agent units.

Box memory beyond 16 GiB: a box may have any memory in 256 MiB steps up to its runner's memory budget (at most 65536 MiB). Runners advertise that budget in the new capability max_guest_memory_v2_mib and keep max_guest_memory_mib at no more than 16384 MiB, so older controllers and agents accept their heartbeats; a controller sends sizes above 16384 MiB or off the old power-of-two list only to runners that advertise the new capability. The dashboard offers 32 and 64 GiB (dashboard UI 1.0.1). New controller setting limits.box_memory_mib (default 0: no pool-wide cap) caps the memory a box may be created or resized to, live with ow config set; existing boxes above a lowered cap still start and fork. Protocol, catalog schema, runtime and host layout are unchanged. Class 2: the worker restarts behind the capture gate.

Event logs: when telemetry.forward_endpoint is set, the controller forwards every node and controller event as an OTLP log record through the existing bounded in-memory forwarder: channel connect, disconnect and reconnect with reason classes, session open and close, agent and controller starts and upgrades, worker restarts, every worker operation: agent jobs, the controller's own worker and the scheduled recovery points with their seals and results, handed to the agent or controller over an owner-only local socket (box lifecycle, recovery captures and seals) with op, outcome, duration, hashed box ID and error class, and alert transitions. No command, file content, environment value, box name or worker error text is sent. New controller settings telemetry.logs (default true) and telemetry.log_level (info|warn|error) take effect within 3 s; runners advertise telemetry_logs_v1. Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged. Class-1 upgrade: controller and agents restart; boxes keep running.

Dashboard UI bundles: the dashboard serves its browser UI from a separately released, hash-checked bundle (ow-dashboard-ui-<version>.tar.gz, tag dashboard-ui-v<version>) chosen by the new controller setting dashboard.ui_bundle (default builtin), or from the copy built into ow. ow dashboard-ui install|list keeps verified bundles under <data>/dashboard-ui/; ow config set dashboard.ui_bundle switches or rolls back from the next page load with no restart, and refuses a missing, damaged or API-incompatible bundle. A bundle that stops qualifying falls back to the built-in UI with a visible reason. New GET /api/version (dashboard API 1, capability dashboard_ui_bundle_v1); routes, CSP, headers and authentication are unchanged. Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged. Class-1 upgrade: the dashboard restarts alone, once; later UI updates need no core release.

waivers.worker: crates/ow/src/host.rs adds only the local ow dashboard-ui CLI arm; no worker code, operation, runtime or service changes.

releases.notes: Upgrader capture gate: disk-only recovery points (0.9.40 on) hold no RAM state and always boot cold, so they no longer count as captures the target cannot resume. Before, every class-2 upgrade of a host with such points was refused unless --accept-cold. Takes effect from the next upgrade, since an upgrade runs the installed upgrader. No unit restarts.

Upgrader: after the pin switch the new worker is quiesced as soon as it answers, before the agent and gateway start, and stays quiesced until verify passes; rollback starts the old worker the same way. The resume step lifts it, and a lift that fails leaves the journal at resume for recover. Before, a wake on connection could reach the new worker during verify, and a large box's resume (its hibernation snapshot is hashed first) held the one-request worker past verify's deadline, so the upgrade rolled back while that resume still held the box and the rollback's stop timed out. The worker unit's stop (`down --hibernate --wait`, no stop timeout) now retries until every box is hibernated, starts still refused, instead of giving up after 840 s or on a busy box and letting systemd kill the running VMs; a box that can never be hibernated now holds the stop until an operator acts. The upgrader fix takes effect from the next upgrade, since an upgrade runs the installed upgrader. Class-2 worker cycle (the worker unit changes); protocol, catalog, runtime and host layout 2 unchanged.

Per-box AWS roles in metadata mode (opt-in, "mode": "metadata" in aws-identity.json; web identity stays the default): the controller assumes each attached role under the IAM path /ow-box/ of its own account with its EC2 instance role (explicit instance-metadata credentials, session tags ow-box and ow-owner, source identity, one hour, refreshed with 30 minutes left and kept fresh for hibernated boxes), outside the catalog lock, and pushes the credentials to the box's runner through a new aws-creds worker operation. The worker keeps them in memory only and serves them at 169.254.169.254 (IMDSv2 only, HMAC tokens bound to box, VMM and role generation, per-box connection and rate limits, hop limit 1 by default, no CORS, X-Forwarded-For refused, never the real instance metadata) from its own threads through an nft prerouting redirect; boxes without a role get an immediate 404. Detach, re-attach, transfer and allow-list removal withdraw the runner's copy before the change commits; a running box with a role on an unreachable runner cannot be transferred. Workers advertise aws_metadata_v1. The refresher now always runs, so turning access on or switching its mode needs no restart. A live-box attachment waits for STS outside the catalog lock and worker credential acknowledgement before success; failed or superseded delivery returns an error, while stopped/parked attachments remain pending. Additive catalog columns aws_roles.hop_limit and aws_roles.served, plus aws_role_generations and its delete trigger retaining generation high-water marks across detach, transfer and controller restart in both modes; catalog schema 7, worker interface 3, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged. The AWS component gains boxRoles (host role may assume role/ow-box/* only). Class-2 worker upgrade; runners without aws_metadata_v1 never receive credentials.

Node telemetry over OpenTelemetry (docs/TELEMETRY.md). Node agents advertise telemetry_v1 and, once the controller's acknowledgement offers the telemetry-v1 extension, send OTLP/HTTP JSON metrics (host CPU, memory, load, data-volume space, agent and worker memory, per-box memory of at most 32 boxes under opaque IDs, channel connects and disconnects, capture and restore timings) and events (channel disconnected/reconnected with a reason class, agent start, operations) over the existing node channel, at most 28 KiB per frame, from a bounded 64-payload queue that drops the oldest and counts it. The controller validates each frame, stamps the authenticated node, keeps the latest summary and a 200-event ring per node in additive tables (settings, config_changes, node_telemetry, node_events; no schema bump), raises node_offline and disk_low alerts (journal line and event on each transition), and forwards everything to telemetry.forward_endpoint when set. Settings live on the controller only: ow config list|get|set (telemetry.enabled, telemetry.interval_s, telemetry.forward_endpoint, alerts.offline_after_s, alerts.disk_low_gib), versioned and recorded, carried on every acknowledgement so runners apply a change within about 3 s. ow health prints fleet health and exits 1 on an alert; ow nodes adds alerts and telemetry; the dashboard shows an alert banner and a health line per host to the pool owner. Old agents ignore the extra acknowledgement field and send nothing; new agents send nothing to an old controller. Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel, host layout 2 and stage 0 are unchanged; the worker is untouched.

waivers.worker: crates/ow/src/host.rs adds only the local ow health and ow config CLI arms and annotates ow nodes output; no worker code, operation, runtime or service changes.

releases.notes: Automatic recovery points of running boxes are disk-only: the guest is paused only while its disk is reflinked and no RAM is written, removing the full-RAM write from that pause (real-runner pause duration remains unmeasured); such a point restores as a cold boot (its manifest says disk_only and names no CPU, so an older worker refuses to resume it). The controller runs every catalog/health call off its async threads over reused connections and never holds the session lock across one; each runner writes transient health in its own private SQLite WAL file, while the live_nodes view preserves durable catalog policy and revocation. Upgrade controller and gateway together, since older gateways read only catalog heartbeats; a session whose mark or heartbeat cannot be recorded (an error, or no matching row) ends with a log line so the agent reconnects, and a controller stall no longer drops every session. The agent reconnects after 20 s without a frame from the controller, skips DNS for IP literals and reuses the last resolved addresses while lookups hang. Runners whose worker and agent have this advertise recovery_disk_only_v1.

Moved, forked and woken (managed) boxes now delete, resize (stopped; CPU, RAM, disk growth), snapshot, delete named snapshots and change public SSH keys under their committed placement epoch. A managed delete leaves a worker tombstone (fence cleaned, no export or import intent) that refuses every later request, and the agent may repeat a lost managed delete or snapshot delete against it; the controller then deletes the fenced copies on runners the box was moved or parked from the same way, before dropping the box (an offline one refuses with its name, and the retry finishes). A deleted fork child's imported capture is removed when its parent has no live copy on that runner, and a capture still sealing when its box is deleted is never committed. The worker's snapshot inventory reports disk_bytes, from which the controller fills in snapshots recorded without a size so they publish too. Workers advertise managed_lifecycle_v1; the controller refuses managed deletes on runners without it. The controller's recovery loop publishes named snapshots of managed boxes to the artifact store once, rehomes a published snapshot to the store when its box leaves that runner and then removes the old runner's copy; a fork from a stored snapshot imports its artifact on any runner without a new capture, and snapshot listings show the artifact ID for managed restore. Catalog schema 7, worker interface 3, protocol, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged. Class-2 worker upgrade; until a runner's worker is upgraded, managed deletes there are refused and its snapshot copies stay.

AWS component input poolAdmins (Host only; login emails) sets the gateway config's pool_admins on the controller's dashboard, so pool admins are managed in place; it needs a dashboard and admits nobody by itself. The config parameter carries dashboard.poolAdmins and ow-host writes OW_POOL_ADMINS to dashboard.env only when set, so hosts without it render the same env file; the changed dashboard-prepare restarts each dashboard once on upgrade, and setting or changing poolAdmins later restarts only the dashboard. Dashboard and controller logins are now matched in full, so a trailing newline is refused. Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel, host layout 2 and stage 0 are unchanged.

Optional per-box AWS access: the controller acts as an OIDC identity provider (ES256 key, discovery document and JWKS) and, for boxes with an operator-allowed role attached, signs 15-minute identity tokens with one key per box generation; a move, fork, ownership transfer or detach withdraws the old key from the JWKS so its tokens stop verifying. The worker writes them into running guests on tmpfs through a new aws-token operation (ow exec on images without dev and the terminal agent export them too) that never wakes a box or restarts its idle clock; the AWS SDK chain calls AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity itself. Off unless aws-identity.json exists. Additive catalog table aws_roles; catalog schema 7, worker interface 3, runtime, guest kernel and host layout remain unchanged. Class-2 worker upgrade; runners without aws_identity_v1 report the role as not delivered.

Pool admins (gateway config `pool_admins`, login emails; default none) and owners manage box ownership. New `ow transfer BOX --to EMAIL [--keep-access]` (API op `transfer`, dashboard Transfer action) moves a box and the snapshots its owner took of it to another owner in one catalog transaction: physical ID, disk, placement, previews, SSH keys and running state stay, with no worker contact. Owner or pool admin only; the new owner's name space and limits must have room; grants end and the old owner keeps an admin share only with --keep-access. `ow create --owner EMAIL` (pool admins) and `ow fork BOX CHILD --owner EMAIL` (owner or pool admin, including cross-runner and managed forks) make the box in that owner's name space and limits. Transfer also moves the owner's stored captures and snapshot artifacts. Pool admins see other owners' boxes in the dashboard to fork or transfer them. Every ownership change is recorded in an additive `audit` table, shown to the actor and both owners (`ow audit`, dashboard Ownership changes). Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7 (additive table), runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged. Class-1 controller and dashboard upgrade; no worker restart.

waivers.worker: crates/ow/src/host.rs adds only local CLI refusal arms for transfer, audit and --owner; no worker code, operation, runtime or service changes.

releases.notes: S3 calls use the AWS SDK for Rust and its refreshing credential chain with pooled connections, bounded parallel transfers and retries. Recovery points use 32 MiB SHA-256 chunks (sha256-chunks-32m-v2), reading changed reflink extents and uploading while sealing in one pass; 8 MiB chunk seals and whole-file backups remain readable. Recovery client sealing is capability negotiated; older clients use worker sealing. Artifact multipart uploads and ETag-pinned ranged downloads run in parallel; interrupted response bodies retry. Retention and GC semantics, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel and host layout remain unchanged. Class-2 worker and agent upgrade; upgrade restore readers before using new recovery points.

waivers.dashboard: Only a refusal test adds recovery-seal to private worker operations; dashboard behavior is unchanged.

releases.notes: Cross-runner fork and move refusals say why: the controller names the runner and the reason (offline or draining, no artifact store, stale or exhausted disk headroom, worker without move/fork support, taken child name, unfinished transfer or pending operation, snapshot not of this box) instead of a generic error, and records the refusal as a failed operation with error_code refused that ow status lists; the same operation key returns the same refusal. Class 1: controller only; protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged.

Dashboard dialogs: name fields validate in the browser again (the name pattern no longer fails to compile), naming the allowed characters. A dialog shows its result and unlocks as soon as the operation answers instead of waiting for the state reload. A non-JSON 5xx from the proxy says the server is not answering instead of asking to sign in again. Dialog errors clear on retry, the submit button shows progress (Capturing…), and notices clear on Cancel and on view or machine switch; a result is shown only where its operation started. Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged. Class-1 upgrade: the dashboard restarts alone.

Serial exec stops commands after 30 s, including developer-user commands, and cleans up their process group before the next command. Developer login shells retain the command process group. The console explains the limit, keeps command output isolated and avoids extra blank lines before exit status. Protocols, catalog schema, runtime, guest kernel and host layout are unchanged.

Plain refusal reasons: a fork that does not fit on its parent's runner is refused with error code fork_capacity and a sentence naming the runner and the fork's shape (catalog admission, same-runner managed fork reservation, or the worker's own reservation limit); sharing a machine with your own login is refused with error code already_owner. The dashboard shows both without operation or retry-key details; the CLI shows the same text. Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged. Class-1 upgrade: the controller and dashboard restart; workers and guests are untouched.

Card content is top-aligned; delete and restore confirms use a danger button under a "CANNOT BE UNDONE" eyebrow; resizing to the current disk size answers "Already N GiB" in the dialog without sending an operation; the page notice is spaced from the card below; on phone widths a card tap scrolls the selected-machine actions into view. Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged. Class-1 dashboard upgrade; no worker restart.

Dashboard recovery status and snapshot list: machine cards show the last durable point as relative time (full time on hover), a machine under an hour old without a point reads "First recovery point pending" in neutral text, and the warning colour appears only once the one-hour target is missed or an upload error is reported. The controller's state gives machines created_at, and a failed capture its machine and failed_at from its snapshot operation. The worker records the child a live fork's capture was taken for in the capture manifest (optional field fork, also in the snapshots reply); older readers ignore it, older captures lack it and read "Taken for a fork". Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged. Class 2 in place: the normal quiesce/swap/resume upgrade restarts the worker with the dashboard and controller.

Dashboard keeps keyboard focus on the same machine card or action button when the 5 s refresh rebuilds the lists. Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged. Class-1 upgrade: the dashboard restarts; workers and guests are untouched.

Host reserve: each AWS host keeps CPU and RAM box admission never claims, 1 vCPU and 2 GiB on a Host, 0.5 vCPU and 1 GiB on a runner (hostReserveCpuMillis, hostReserveMemoryMib). The host subtracts it from logical CPUs before the vcpuOvercommit ratio and from RAM, for the worker budget, the local controller and runner invitations. The controller/agent unit moves into owcontrol.slice (CPUWeight 1000, MemoryMin/MemoryLow, OOMScoreAdjust -900); the worker and its VMs into owguests.slice (MemoryMax host RAM less the reserve). Every Linux worker also caps OW_MAX_MEMORY_MIB and OW_MAX_VCPUS at host capacity less OW_HOST_RESERVE_CPU_MILLIS/OW_HOST_RESERVE_MEMORY_MIB (default a runner's; ow host up starts its worker with a controller host's) times OW_VCPU_OVERCOMMIT, refuses to start when nothing is left, and starts each VMM with OOM score 500 in a guests cgroup under a delegated worker unit (worker -900, CPU weight 1000, memory.low). apply refuses a reserve that leaves no room for boxes. The worker reports the reserve and ow nodes shows host_reserve (cpu_millis, memory_mib, disk_gib). The node agent builds heartbeats on its status thread and writes its status files on another, so a long capture, a cache hash or a slow disk no longer makes a runner look offline; a beat not refreshed for 1500 s closes the channel. A signal interrupting a worker request (a child process exiting) no longer drops the channel. Class 2 in place: apply stages the units and budget, the normal quiesce/swap/resume upgrade applies them; a running box beyond the lowered CPU budget stays hibernated until capacity frees. A host-to-runner conversion must carry the host's reserve. Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged; no stage 0 change.

Dashboard copy and counters for a shared host pool. Footer and sidebar name the shared private host pool; the pool banner says who can see guest data and the invitation policy appears only in the invite dialog. The memory counter shows the owner's provisioned usage against their owner limits (machines, vCPU, memory, disk); the usage view labels pool memory as shared by all users. A failed first state load shows a retry in the machine grid and keeps New machine disabled. Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged. Class-1 upgrade: the dashboard restarts alone.

Fork/delete robustness and honest disk admission. Worker disk admission subtracts each box's unwritten bytes (logical size minus allocated blocks), not its full logical size, from real free space, plus the host reserve; status adds free_disk_bytes and unwritten_disk_bytes, shown by ow nodes as disk.free_bytes and disk.unwritten_bytes; cache staging and eviction use the same accounting. A plain snapshot or live fork resumes the guest after the RAM/state save and disk reflink and hashes on a separate worker thread, so other requests are served meanwhile; replies carry timings.paused_ms and timings.total_ms. VMMs boot and load with Firecracker dirty-page tracking; a capture saves only RAM pages changed since that VMM's last boot, load or capture (Diff) and lays them over a reflink of the previous memory image after resume, so published memory files stay complete images; recovery-point chunk seals reuse unchanged memory chunks. A RAM save invalidates the prior base before contacting the VMM; disk-copy, resume or merge failure forces a full RAM save on retry, then incremental captures resume against the repaired base. A live fork of a stopped or hibernated box is refused upfront (controller and worker); a failed fork removes its capture and a failed create its partial directory; delete of an ID the worker never registered removes the directory an interrupted create or fork left, and the controller sends that delete before dropping a never-made machine's row. The worker durably associates a generated live-fork capture with its pending child before capture begins, so deletion after interruption removes both the partial child and its capture, even if the child directory was never created; deletion cancels publication and queued creation, and cleanup errors retain the association for retry. The controller marks a rejected fork's child failed (unmade: true) and releases it, fails an uncertain create or fork its runner still lacks after 30 minutes, and deletes a never-made machine the runner does not list from the catalog only. ow delete names the snapshots that go with a box and asks first (--yes without a terminal); the dashboard delete dialog lists them. Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged. Class-2 upgrade: the worker restarts through the existing upgrade policy.

New `ow rename BOX NEW_NAME` (remote API op `rename`, dashboard Rename action) changes only the logical name of a machine its owner holds: physical ID, disk, snapshots, placement, sharing grants, published ports, SSH keys and running state stay, with no worker contact. Owner only; the new name follows the create rules and must be free for that owner; a machine in a move, park, wake or fork transfer refuses it until the transfer ends. Idempotent with --operation-key; renaming to the same name is a no-op. Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged. Class-1 controller and dashboard upgrade; no worker restart.

releases.notes: Recovery points read and send only what changed. The worker seals each managed recovery point under the digest of its 8 MiB chunk list (chunks.json beside the manifest; manifest digest sha256-chunks-8m-v1), taking a chunk from the last durable point's seal unread when both files map it to the same physical extents and treating holes as zero chunks; verification of such a snapshot still reads every byte. The uploader sends missing chunks with up to eight parallel in-process signed requests (credentials exported once from the AWS CLI chain), lists the store's chunks once per point in parallel (recorded in RUNNER/recovery-index) instead of checking each chunk, records each upload as it lands so a killed run resumes, and sends again any chunk missing from the store, also for a point whose manifest is already stored. Restores of chunked points download in parallel. Each run prints capture and transfer counts per point. Older readers cannot verify chunk-sealed points; upgrade the CLI used for restore first. New `ow delete-snapshot BOX NAME` deletes one named snapshot through the controller (worker flag snapshot_delete_v1; older runners refuse it before dispatch). Protocol, worker interface 3, catalog schema 7, runtime, guest kernel and host layout 2 are unchanged. Use the normal class-2 worker upgrade; no timer, unit or stage 0 change.

Host staging (first install and ow-host upgrade) installs the pinned release's published Linux ow and, on worker hosts, the newly published ow-guest-linux-amd64, after checking them against the release's SHA256SUMS and source-commit.txt (exact tag and commit); a checksum or commit mismatch is refused before anything is written. A commit that is not the release tag, a missing asset, a non-GitHub repository or --from-source builds on the host as before, and the log names the path. Upgrades run by this or a later ow-host use it; an older ow-host staging this release still builds it. No unit, protocol, catalog, runtime, guest kernel or stage 0 change; no restart.

Opt-in RunnerPool component and controller-host adapter (ow-host pool). New infrastructure only: an unchanged consumer stack gets no new instance and no host replacement; bootstrap.sh, stage 0 and existing Host/Runner resources are unchanged. ow_host.py gains pool-runner identity (node from its data volume) and a join request through a per-instance secret; existing host and runner configs validate and render as before. The controller scaler accepts an opt-in live mode, refused unless a private recovery-drill attestation and a passing provider check for every pool exist; it then makes only newly recorded actions effectful for the adapter to execute and settle by receipt. Shadow configs behave as before. No agent, worker, catalog schema (7, reader floor 7), runtime or CPU ratio change.

Component inputs dataVolumeIops and dataVolumeThroughput set the data volume's gp3 performance; unset keeps the current volume unchanged. EBS applies a size or performance change online, and the host's existing apply step grows the Btrfs filesystem. Component only: runtime, worker and host protocols, catalog schema 7 and reader floor 7, guest kernel, host layout and stage 0 are unchanged; no restart, transfer or guest-state change is required.

Opt-in controller shadow planning with read-only runner inventory refresh, conditional session/placement-bound state and durability observations, and maximum liability forecasts. Only unexecuted shadow forecasts expire at cooldown; effectful or uncertain reservations remain held. Schema 7 and reader floor 7 require private backup and coordinated catalog-reader upgrade. No live provider executor, automatic drain, worker/runtime/guest/kernel/layout or CPU ratio change.
